title: Rotation Engagement Handbook and Status Automation Guide
author: Asha Patel
content:
Purpose
-------
This handbook codifies Redwood Inference’s approach to on-call rotations, incident classification, runbook structure, postmortem practice, and automated status page communications. It is intended for SREs, service owners, engineers, support, and product managers who participate in incident mitigation and outward communications.

Scope
-----
Applies to: all production-facing Redwood services (hosted API, dedicated control plane, private deploy agents). Excludes experimental sandbox clusters unless their failure can affect customer-facing capacity.

Key principles
--------------
- Safety first: protect customer data and restore availability; mitigation > perfection.
- Clear roles: Incident Commander (IC), Communications Lead, Primary Engineer, Secondary / Escalation.
- Timeboxing: accelerate triage, minimize cognitive load with templates and automation.
- Learning: every Sev1/Sev2 incident requires a postmortem with action items and owners.

Severity taxonomy and SLO guardrails
-----------------------------------
- Sev1 (P0): Production service unavailable or correctness severely degraded for > 2 minutes; customer-impacting across multiple customers or critical customers. Target response: page within 2 min, mitigation path within 15 min.
- Sev2 (P1): Significant degradation for a subset of customers or major feature (e.g., streaming broken) with customer workarounds. Target response: page within 15 min, mitigation within 1 hour.
- Sev3 (P2): Minor degradation, non-urgent bugs, or single-customer impact with workarounds. Follow regular operational cadence.

Representative SLOs (exposed in SLO dashboard)
------------------------------------------------
- Hosted API availability: 99.95% monthly for production region endpoints.
- Median (p50) inference latency for short prompts: < 200 ms; p95 < 1200 ms.
- Control plane API success rate: 99.9% over 24h.

Incident lifecycle: quick-run checklist
--------------------------------------
1) Detect & Page: Alerts route to on-call (PagerDuty) with runbook link.
2) Triage (0–10m): Determine severity, impact, and immediate mitigation (e.g., rollback, scaling).
3) Assign roles (10m): IC, Primary Engineer, Communications Lead, SRE support.
4) Mitigate (15–60m): Apply mitigation steps until service is acceptably degraded or recovered.
5) Stabilize (60–240m): Post-mortem draft, hotfix rollout and verification.
6) Close & document (24–72h): Finalize postmortem, complete action items.

Runbook template (required header for all runbooks)
---------------------------------------------------
Every runbook must start with these fields:
- runbook_id: short dashed identifier (e.g., runtime-gpu-oom)
- service_owner: team name and primary contact
- pager_policy: who is paged and escalation windows
- severity_association: default severity mapping
- impact_checks: short list of queries to confirm impact
- safe_mitigation: list of mitigations that are reversible

Example runbook: inference-runtime-high-cpu
-----------------------------------------
Summary: High CPU on inference runtime nodes causing elevated latency and request queueing.
Impact checks:
- Grafana: inference-runtime/cpu_utilization > 90% (5m)
- Alerts: recurrence of queue_backlog > 200 requests
- Customer reports: ticket/Slack channel #support-api showing 4+ reports in 10 min
Immediate safe mitigation (in order):
1) Increase replica count (k8s HPA override): kubectl -n inference patch deployment runtime --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":5}]'
2) Scale up GPU pool (infra-ops): runbook-scripts/scale-gpu-pool --cluster-prod --count +2
3) Unload large batch jobs: identify active jobs and trigger graceful drain: curl -X POST $ADMIN_API/jobs/drain?job_id=...
4) Apply traffic-shed rule (traffic router): restrict non-critical routes to 10% traffic
Escalation matrix: Primary -> Secondary -> SRE Lead -> On-call Manager.
Post-mitigation checks:
- p95 latency back under threshold for 10 continuous minutes
- No error rate spike in last 5m

Incident roles and responsibilities (concise)
-------------------------------------------
- Incident Commander (IC): owns decisioning and triage step. Usually oncall primary or designated senior engineer.
- Primary Engineer: deepest subject expert for the affected service. Executes runbook steps.
- Secondary / Backup: fills in if Primary unavailable, and prepares rollback plan.
- Communications Lead: owns status page and customer messages, coordinates with customer-success for key accounts.
- Postmortem Author: drafts the timeline and root cause analysis.

Communication templates (status page + customer-facing)
------------------------------------------------------
Use these as starting templates. Replace bracketed fields before publishing.
- Initial public status (short):
  Title: [Major outage] Hosted API: increased latency / partial outage
  Body: We are investigating reports of increased latency affecting text generation in region [us-west-2]. Affected customers may experience delayed or timed-out responses. Our engineers are actively investigating. Next update: in 15 minutes.
- Update (mitigation in place):
  Title: Mitigation applied — traffic routed to fallback model variant
  Body: We have applied a mitigation that routes traffic to a compatible fallback model for a subset of requests to reduce latency while we continue to investigate the root cause. Some requests may receive differences in output quality. We will provide a root cause analysis in the postmortem.
- Resolved:
  Title: Resolved — Hosted API latency issue
  Body: The issue has been resolved. We reverted the temporary routing and verified p95 latency for short prompts is within targets. We will publish a detailed postmortem within 72 hours.

Internal Slack comms template (to #incidents channel)
----------------------------------------------------
[SEV{level}] [service] - short summary\- IC: @handle – Primary: @handle – CL: @handle\- Impact: summary (regions/customers)\- Mitigation: summary\- Next update in 15m or at {time}

Status page automation (example API calls)
-----------------------------------------
We use the Status API (internal) for programmatic updates. Example curl for initial incident post: 

curl -X POST "https://status-internal.redwood.dev/api/v1/incidents" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STATUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"title":"[Investigating] Increased latency in hosted-api-us-west-2","service_ids":["svc-hosted-api-usw2"],"status":"investigating","impact":"partial"}'

Tip: integrate the above into incident responders (PagerDuty webhooks) so an alert automatically posts a skeleton incident that IC can edit.

Postmortem checklist and template
--------------------------------
Required for Sev1/Sev2. Document the following as plain text in the postmortem doc:
- Incident ID and timeline (UTC timestamps)
- Detection path (monitoring, customer report, CI)
- Impact summary and customers affected
- Root cause analysis (what failed and why)
- Remediation and long-term fix plan with owners and due dates
- Action items tracked in backlog; link to ticket(s)
- Severity assessment and SLO impact calculations (token counts, error minutes)
- Lessons learned and follow-up game-day exercise suggestion

Minimum postmortem delivery windows:
- Draft: within 72 hours of incident resolution
- Finalized with reviewers: within 7 calendar days

Rotation and scheduling policy (practical rules)
-----------------------------------------------
- Rotation length: 1 week (Mon 00:00 UTC — Sun 23:59 UTC) for primary oncall. Secondary rotation offset by 1 week.
- Handover notes: outgoing oncall must publish a 10-minute handoff summary in the oncall board including outstanding incidents, maintenance windows, and infra churn.
- Time off & exemptions: request 14 days ahead. For extended leave (> 4 weeks), team adjusts rotation or assigns merchant oncall.
- Escalation fast path: if primary does not acknowledge page within 5 minutes, PD escalates to secondary. If no ack in 15 minutes, escalate to SRE Lead.

On-call fatigue and safety measures
----------------------------------
- Nighttime escalation limits: high-frequency non-critical alerts are grouped and swept at 06:00 local unless a human indicates immediate need.
- Silent-maintenance windows: planned changes that may trigger alerts must include a maintenance window in PD to suppress notifications.
- Incident credit & compensations: engineers receive an incident-response credit for severe incidents (tracked by people-ops).

Game days and simulation blueprint
----------------------------------
Goal: validate runbooks, automation, rotas, and communications under pressure.
Frequency: quarterly for platform-wide, monthly for critical services.
Sample half-day agenda (4 hours)
1) Kickoff (15m): objectives and rules of engagement.
2) Scenario execution (90m): seeded synthetic failure (e.g., control-plane DB latency spike).
3) Observability & mitigation (60m): participants execute runbooks and post status updates.
4) Debrief (45m): what worked, what failed, action items assigned.
Deliverables: runbook updates, automation tweaks, and an executive summary submitted to leadership.

Metrics we track for oncall health and incident quality
------------------------------------------------------
- Mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Sev1: target < 2 min.
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM): target < 20 min for Sev1.
- Postmortem completion rate within 7d: 100% for Sev1, 90% for Sev2.
- Number of false-positive high-priority alerts per quarter (goal < 5).

Operational tooling and recommended automations
---------------------------------------------
- PagerDuty integration: automated escalation policies and PD -> Status API webhook.
- Incident skeleton creation: webhook places a draft incident and runbook link in the incident doc store.
- Automated runbook health checks: weekly synthetic probes that exercise the mitigation steps (e.g., run the scale-gpu-pool script in dry-run).
- Postmortem stub automation: when an incident closes, create a postmortem stub in the docs with required sections prefilled.

Ownership and governance
------------------------
- Oncall program lead: SRE Manager (operational ownership for rotation rules and tooling).
- Incident policy owner: Head of Reliability (policy approval and SLA alignment).
- Runbook shepherds: each service owner is responsible for their runbooks and must review them quarterly.

Appendices
---------
A) Quick comms cheatsheet
- When to use customer-facing status: any Sev1 or customer-impacting Sev2.
- Use internal-only Slack for triage details. Always keep the public status non-technical.

B) Example escalation command snippets
- Check runtime pods: kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=inference-runtime -o wide
- Tail logs: kubectl -n inference logs -f pod/inference-runtime-abc123

C) Postmortem rubric (how reviewers score the document)
- Completeness (timeline, impact) 0–5
- Root cause clarity 0–5
- Actionability (concrete fixes with owners) 0–5
- Communication quality (timeliness of status updates) 0–5

D) Contact matrix (rotating oncall aliases)
- primary-oncall@redwood.dev (PagerDuty alias)
- secondary-oncall@redwood.dev
- ops-cs@redwood.dev (customer success)

Document maintenance
--------------------
- This handbook is reviewed quarterly by the oncall program lead and after every Sev1. Runbook owners should confirm runbook accuracy at least once per quarter.

Related resources
-----------------
- Incident command playbook and escalation matrix (linked in related_pages)
- Oncall simulation cookbook (game day scenarios)
- SLO & error budget dashboards

End of document
